translations.literal: Melting one thousand coins yielded six jin of copper; casting vessels, one jin yielded six hundred coins; therefore melters and casters were many and coin ever more depleted.
translations.idiomatic: A thousand coins melted to six jin of copper, but one jin cast into vessels yielded six hundred coins' worth—so melting proliferated and coin grew scarcer.

sentences.zh: 判度支趙贊採連州白銅鑄大錢，一當十，以權輕重。

translations.literal: Acting Expenditure Commissioner Zhao Zan mined Lianzhou white copper to cast large coin, one equal to ten, to balance light and heavy.
translations.idiomatic: Acting Expenditure Commissioner Zhao Zan minted large coins from Lianzhou white copper, valued at ten-for-one, to stabilize exchange rates.

sentences.zh: 貞元初，駱谷、散關禁行人以一錢出者。

translations.literal: Early in Zhenyuan, Luogu and San Pass forbade travelers from taking out even one coin.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenyuan, Luogu and San Pass barred travelers from carrying even a single coin out.

sentences.zh: 諸道鹽鐵使張滂奏禁江淮鑄銅為器，惟鑄鑑而已。

translations.literal: Circuit Salt Commissioner Zhang Pang memorialized to forbid Jiang-Huai casting copper into vessels, allowing mirrors only.
translations.idiomatic: Circuit Commissioner Zhang Pang petitioned to ban Jiang-Huai copper vessels except mirrors.

sentences.zh: 十年，詔天下鑄銅器，每器一斤，其直不得過百六十，銷錢者以盜鑄論。

translations.literal: In the tenth year an edict ordered casting copper vessels under Heaven; each vessel one jin, price not exceeding one hundred sixty; melting coin was prosecuted as illicit casting.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year an edict permitted copper vessels of one jin maximum at one hundred sixty cash, with coin melting punished as counterfeiting.

sentences.zh: 然而民間錢益少，繒帛價輕，州縣禁錢不出境，商賈皆絕。

translations.literal: Yet among the people coin grew ever fewer, silk prices light; prefectures and counties forbade coin leaving their borders; merchants all ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Yet coin grew scarcer, silk prices fell, prefectures blocked coin from leaving their borders, and commerce stalled.

sentences.zh: 浙西觀察使李若初請通錢往來，而京師商賈齎錢四方貿易者，不可勝計。

translations.literal: Zhexi Observation Commissioner Li Ruochu requested allowing coin to circulate; yet capital merchants carrying coin to trade in the four directions were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Zhexi Commissioner Li Ruochu petitioned to allow coin circulation, while capital merchants trading coin nationwide were beyond count.

sentences.zh: 詔復禁之。

translations.literal: An edict again forbade it.
translations.idiomatic: An edict reimposed the ban.

sentences.zh: 二十年，命市井交易，以綾、羅、絹、布、雜貨與錢兼用。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year market transactions were ordered to use damask, gauze, silk, cloth, and miscellaneous goods together with coin.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year markets were required to accept damask, gauze, silk, cloth, and goods alongside coin.

sentences.zh: 憲宗以錢少復禁用銅器。

translations.literal: Xianzong, because coin was scarce, again forbade copper vessels.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong, with coin scarce, again banned copper vessels.

sentences.zh: 時商賈至京師，委錢諸道進奏院及諸軍、諸使富家，以輕裝趨四方，合券乃取之，號「飛錢」。

translations.literal: At that time merchants arriving at the capital deposited coin with circuit memorial offices and wealthy households of armies and commissioners; with light baggage they hastened to the four directions and redeemed vouchers to receive it—called "flying money."
translations.idiomatic: Merchants in the capital deposited funds with circuit memorial offices and army brokers, traveled light to trade nationwide, and redeemed vouchers for payment—called "flying money."

sentences.zh: 京兆尹裴武請禁與商賈飛錢者，廋索諸坊，十人為保。

translations.literal: Metropolitan Prefect Pei Wu requested forbidding flying money with merchants; search all wards; ten people formed a mutual-guarantee group.
translations.idiomatic: Metropolitan Prefect Pei Wu petitioned to ban flying-money transactions, searching all wards with ten-person mutual-guarantee groups.

sentences.zh: 鹽鐵使李巽以郴州平陽銅坑二百八十餘，復置桂陽監，以兩鑪日鑄錢二十萬。

translations.literal: Salt Commissioner Li Xun, because Chenzhou's Pingyang had over two hundred eighty copper pits, restored the Guiyang mint; with two furnaces daily cast two hundred thousand coins.
translations.idiomatic: Salt Commissioner Li Xun, citing over 280 copper pits at Chenzhou's Pingyang, restored the Guiyang mint with two furnaces casting 200,000 coins daily.

sentences.zh: 天下歲鑄錢十三萬五千緡。

translations.literal: Under Heaven yearly casting was one hundred thirty-five thousand strings.
translations.idiomatic: Annual nationwide minting totaled 135,000 strings.

sentences.zh: 命商賈蓄錢者，皆出以市貨；

translations.literal: Merchants hoarding coin were ordered to release it all to buy goods;
translations.idiomatic: Merchants hoarding coin were ordered to spend it on goods;

sentences.zh: 天下有銀之山必有銅，唯銀無益於人，五嶺以北，採銀一兩者流他州，官吏論罪。

translations.literal: wherever under Heaven there were silver mountains there was copper; only silver benefited people little; north of the Five Ridges, one who mined one liang of silver was exiled to another prefecture and officials were prosecuted.
translations.idiomatic: where silver mountains existed copper was also found; silver alone was deemed of little public benefit—north of the Five Ridges, mining even one liang meant exile, with officials punished.

sentences.zh: 元和四年，京師用錢緡少二十及有鉛錫錢者，捕之；

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yuanhe, in the capital strings short twenty and those with lead-tin coin were seized;
translations.idiomatic: In 809 the capital seized short strings and lead-tin coin;

sentences.zh: 非交易而錢行衢路者，不問。

translations.literal: those carrying coin in streets without transaction were not questioned.
translations.idiomatic: but coin carried in streets without active trade was not penalized.

sentences.zh: 復詔采五嶺銀坑，禁錢出嶺。

translations.literal: An edict again ordered mining Five Ridges silver pits and forbade coin leaving the ranges.
translations.idiomatic: An edict reopened Five Ridges silver mining and barred coin from leaving the region.

sentences.zh: 六年，貿易錢十緡以上者，參用布帛。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, trade of ten strings or more was to use cloth and silk in part.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year transactions over ten strings required partial payment in cloth and silk.

sentences.zh: 蔚州三河冶距飛狐故監二十里而近，河東節度使王鍔置鑪，疏拒馬河水鑄錢，工費尤省，以刺史李聽為使，以五鑪鑄，每鑪月鑄錢三十萬，自是河東錫錢皆廢。

translations.literal: Weizhou's Sanhe smeltery was within twenty li of the old Feihu mint; Hedong military governor Wang E set up furnaces, channeled Juma River water to cast coin with especially low labor cost; Prefect Li Ting was made commissioner; with five furnaces casting, each furnace monthly cast three hundred thousand coins; from this Hedong tin coin was all abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Weizhou's Sanhe smeltery lay twenty li from the old Feihu mint. Hedong governor Wang E built furnaces using Juma River waterpower, with Prefect Li Ting overseeing five furnaces each producing 300,000 coins monthly—ending Hedong tin coin entirely.

sentences.zh: 自京師禁飛錢，家有滯藏，物價寖輕。

translations.literal: Since the capital forbade flying money, households had stagnant hoards and prices gradually fell.
translations.idiomatic: After the capital banned flying money, hoarded coin sat idle and prices gradually fell.

sentences.zh: 判度支盧坦、兵部尚書判戶部事王紹、鹽鐵使王播請許商人於戶部、度支、鹽鐵三司飛錢，每千錢增給百錢，然商人無至者。

translations.literal: Acting Expenditure Commissioner Lu Tan, Minister of War acting for the Ministry of Revenue Wang Shao, and Salt Commissioner Wang Bo requested allowing merchants flying money at the three offices of Revenue, Expenditure, and Salt and Iron, adding one hundred cash per thousand; yet no merchants came.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Tan, Wang Shao, and Wang Bo proposed state-sponsored flying money through the three fiscal offices with a hundred-cash premium per thousand—but no merchants used it.

sentences.zh: 復許與商人敵貫而易之，然錢重帛輕如故。

translations.literal: They again allowed merchants to exchange at par, yet coin remained heavy and silk light as before.
translations.idiomatic: They again allowed merchants to exchange at par, yet coin remained scarce and silk cheap as before.

sentences.zh: 憲宗為之出內庫錢五十萬緡市布帛，每匹加舊估十之一。

translations.literal: Xianzong for this released five hundred thousand strings from the inner treasury to buy cloth and silk, adding one tenth to the old valuation per bolt.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong spent five hundred thousand strings from the inner treasury to buy cloth and silk at ten percent above the old valuation.

sentences.zh: 會吳元濟、王承宗連衡拒命，以七道兵討之，經費屈竭。

translations.literal: When Wu Yuanji and Wang Chengzong allied in defiance, seven-circuit armies were sent against them and expenses were exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Yuanji and Wang Chengzong rebelled in alliance, seven armies were mobilized and the treasury was drained.

sentences.zh: 皇甫鎛建議，內外用錢每緡墊二十外，復抽五十送度支以贍軍。

translations.literal: Huangfu Bo proposed that on top of twenty clipped per string domestically and abroad, fifty more be extracted and sent to Expenditure to support the army.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Bo proposed clipping twenty per string nationwide and extracting fifty more for the army fund.

sentences.zh: 十二年，復給京兆府錢五十萬緡市布帛，而富家錢過五千貫者死，王公重貶，沒入於官，以五之一賞告者。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year five hundred thousand strings were again given the Metropolitan Prefecture to buy cloth and silk; wealthy households with over five thousand strings faced death; princes and dukes with heavy purchases were confiscated; one fifth rewarded informers.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year the metropolitan government received five hundred thousand strings to buy silk; hoarders with over five thousand strings faced death; princes' illicit purchases were confiscated with one-fifth to informers.

sentences.zh: 京師區肆所積，皆方鎮錢，少亦五十萬緡，乃爭市第宅。

translations.literal: What capital wards and markets accumulated was all regional-command money, at least five hundred thousand strings, and they competed to buy mansions.
translations.idiomatic: Capital markets hoarded regional-command coin—at least five hundred thousand strings each—and competed to buy mansions.

sentences.zh: 然富賈倚左右神策軍官錢為名，府縣不敢劾問。

translations.literal: Yet wealthy merchants relied on the name of Left and Right Divine Strategy Army official funds; prefectures and counties dared not investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Wealthy merchants sheltered behind Divine Strategy Army funds, and local officials dared not investigate.

sentences.zh: 民間墊陌有至七十者，鉛錫錢益多，吏捕犯者，多屬諸軍、諸使，謼集市人彊奪，毆傷吏卒。

translations.literal: Among the people clipping reached seventy; lead-tin coin increased ever more; officers seized violators mostly belonging to armies and commissioners; they shouted to market people to seize by force and beat officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Clipping reached seventy percent; lead-tin coin proliferated. Arrested violators were mostly army and commissioner affiliates who incited mobs to assault officers.

sentences.zh: 京兆尹崔元略請犯者本軍、本使涖決，帝不能用，詔送本軍、本使，而京兆府遣人涖決。

translations.literal: Metropolitan Prefect Cui Yuanlue requested that offenders be judged by their own army or commissioner; the emperor could not adopt it; an edict sent them to their army or commissioner, while the Metropolitan Prefecture dispatched people to judge on site.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Cui Yuanlue asked that offenders be tried by their own army or commissioner; the emperor refused, ordering transfer to those units while the metropolitan government still sent officers to adjudicate.

sentences.zh: 穆宗即位，京師鬻金銀十兩亦墊一兩，糴米鹽百錢墊七八。

translations.literal: When Muzong took the throne, in the capital selling ten liang of gold and silver also clipped one liang; buying rice and salt at one hundred cash clipped seven or eight.
translations.idiomatic: When Muzong ascended, capital gold and silver sales clipped one liang per ten, and rice and salt purchases clipped seven or eight per hundred.

sentences.zh: 京兆尹柳公綽以嚴法禁止之。

translations.literal: Metropolitan Prefect Liu Gongchuo forbade it by strict law.
translations.idiomatic: Metropolitan Prefect Liu Gongchuo banned it by strict enforcement.

sentences.zh: 尋以所在用錢墊陌不一，詔從俗所宜，內外給用，每緡墊八十。

translations.literal: Soon because clipping varied by place, an edict followed local custom; domestic and foreign disbursements clipped eighty per string.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, with clipping varying by region, an edict standardized disbursements at eighty percent per string nationwide.

sentences.zh: 寶曆初，河南尹王起請銷錢為佛像者以盜鑄錢論。

translations.literal: Early in Baoli, Henan Prefect Wang Qi requested that those who melted coin for Buddha images be prosecuted as illicit coiners.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Baoli, Henan Prefect Wang Qi petitioned to prosecute melting coin for Buddha images as counterfeiting.

sentences.zh: 大和三年，詔佛像以鉛、錫、土、木為之，飾帶以金銀、鍮石、烏油、藍鐵，唯鑑、磬、釘、鐶、鈕得用銅，餘皆禁之，盜鑄者死。

translations.literal: In the third year of Dahe an edict ordered Buddha images made of lead, tin, earth, and wood; ornament bands of gold, silver, brass, black oil, and blue iron; only mirrors, chimes, nails, rings, and buttons might use copper; the rest were forbidden; illicit casters were put to death.
translations.idiomatic: In 829 an edict required Buddha images of lead, tin, earth, or wood, with gold and silver ornament only; copper was limited to mirrors, chimes, nails, rings, and buttons—counterfeiters faced death.

sentences.zh: 是時峻鉛錫錢之禁，告千錢者賞以五千。

translations.literal: At that time the ban on lead-tin coin was severe; informers on one thousand coins were rewarded five thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Lead-tin coin was strictly banned; informants on one thousand coins received five thousand in reward.

sentences.zh: 四年，詔積錢以七千緡為率，十萬緡者期以一年出之，二十萬以二年。

translations.literal: In the fourth year an edict set hoarded coin at seven thousand strings as the rate; one hundred thousand strings must be released within one year, two hundred thousand within two.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year hoarders of seven thousand strings or more were required to release funds within one year for holdings up to one hundred thousand, two years for two hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 凡交易百緡以上者，匹帛米粟居半。

translations.literal: All transactions of one hundred strings or more were to be half in bolts of silk, cloth, and grain.
translations.idiomatic: Transactions over one hundred strings required half payment in silk, cloth, or grain.

sentences.zh: 河南府、揚州、江陵府以都會之劇，約束如京師。

translations.literal: Henan Prefecture, Yangzhou, and Jiangling Prefecture, because they were bustling metropolises, were regulated like the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Henan Prefecture, Yangzhou, and Jiangling, as major commercial hubs, were regulated like the capital.

sentences.zh: 未幾皆罷。

translations.literal: Before long all were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Soon all these measures were repealed.

sentences.zh: 八年，河東錫錢復起，鹽鐵使王涯置飛狐鑄錢院於蔚州，天下歲鑄錢不及十萬緡。

translations.literal: In the eighth year Hedong tin coin arose again; Salt Commissioner Wang Ya set up the Feihu mint at Weizhou; yearly casting under Heaven did not reach one hundred thousand strings.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year Hedong tin coin returned; Wang Ya established the Feihu mint at Weizhou; annual nationwide output fell below one hundred thousand strings.

sentences.zh: 文宗病幣輕錢重，詔方鎮縱錢穀交易。

translations.literal: Wenzong lamented that currency was light and coin heavy; an edict allowed regional commands free coin and grain trade.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzong, troubled by cheap goods and dear coin, allowed regional commands free trade in coin and grain.

sentences.zh: 時雖禁銅為器，而江淮、嶺南列肆鬻之，鑄千錢為器，售利數倍。

translations.literal: Although copper vessels were forbidden, Jiang-Huai and Lingnan set up shops to sell them; casting one thousand coins into vessels yielded several times the profit in sale.
translations.idiomatic: Though copper vessels were banned, Jiang-Huai and Lingnan shops sold them openly—melting a thousand coins into vessels yielded several times the profit.

sentences.zh: 宰相李珏請加鑪鑄錢，於是禁銅器，官一切為市之。

translations.literal: Chancellor Li Jue requested adding furnaces to cast coin; thereupon copper vessels were forbidden and the government bought them all.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Li Jue petitioned to expand minting; copper vessels were then banned and bought up by the state.

sentences.zh: 天下銅坑五十，歲采銅二十六萬六千斤。

translations.literal: Copper pits under Heaven numbered fifty; yearly mining was two hundred sixty-six thousand jin of copper.
translations.idiomatic: Fifty copper mines operated nationwide, yielding 266,000 jin annually.

sentences.zh: 及武宗廢浮屠法，永平監官李郁彥請以銅像、鍾、磬、鑪、鐸皆歸巡院，州縣銅益多矣。

translations.literal: When Wuzong abolished the Buddhist law, Yongping mint official Li Yuyan requested that copper images, bells, chimes, censers, and clappers all return to the patrol office; prefectures and counties had ever more copper.
translations.idiomatic: When Wuzong suppressed Buddhism, mint official Li Yuyan petitioned to confiscate copper statues, bells, chimes, censers, and clappers for the patrol office, greatly increasing copper supplies in the prefectures.

sentences.zh: 鹽鐵使以工有常力，不足以加鑄，許諸道觀察使皆得置錢坊。

translations.literal: The Salt Commissioner held that regular labor was insufficient to increase casting; all circuit observation commissioners were permitted to set up mint workshops.
translations.idiomatic: The Salt Commissioner, finding regular labor insufficient for expanded minting, allowed all observation commissioners to establish mint workshops.

sentences.zh: 淮南節度使李紳請天下以州名鑄錢，京師為京錢，大小徑寸，如開元通寶，交易禁用舊錢。

translations.literal: Huainan military governor Li Shen requested casting coin under Heaven by prefecture name; the capital as capital coin, large and small one cun in diameter like Kaiyuan tongbao; old coin forbidden in trade.
translations.idiomatic: Huainan governor Li Shen proposed minting coin named by prefecture—capital coin for the capital, one cun like Kaiyuan tongbao, with old coin banned in trade.

sentences.zh: 會宣宗即位，盡黜會昌之政，新錢以字可辨，復鑄為像。

translations.literal: When Xuanzong took the throne, all Huichang policies were dismissed; new coin distinguishable by inscription was recast into images.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong ascended, Huichang-era policies were reversed; newly distinguishable coin was melted back into Buddhist images.

sentences.zh: 昭宗末，京師用錢八百五十為貫，每百纔八十五，河南府以八十為百云。

translations.literal: Late in Zhaozong, the capital used eight hundred fifty as a string; each hundred was only eighty-five; Henan Prefecture took eighty as one hundred, it was said.
translations.idiomatic: Late under Zhaozong the capital counted eight hundred fifty coins as a full string—only eighty-five per nominal hundred; Henan Prefecture reportedly used eighty as one hundred.
